title: Snowflake
description: A Snowflake account's database, read over Snowflake's SQL API with a programmatic access token or a key pair.

fields.name: account
fields.label: Account
fields.help: Paste the account's URL as Snowflake shows it, or its identifier (myorg-myaccount).

fields.name: auth
fields.label: Sign in with
fields.help: token: a programmatic access token. key-pair: the user's private key.

setup.title: Your Snowflake account
setup.say:
Paste your account's URL as Snowflake shows it — in Snowsight, your name (bottom left) → Account → View account details → Account/Server URL. Its identifier (myorg-myaccount) works too.

If your account lets in only known addresses (a network policy), let the engine's machine in first.

fix.say: That does not look like a Snowflake account. Copy the Account/Server URL from Snowsight (your name → Account → View account details), or write it as myorg-myaccount.
No Snowflake account answers at that address. Check the account URL in Snowsight (your name → Account → View account details); an older account's URL carries its region (xy12345.eu-west-1).

setup.title: A user and role that may only read
setup.say:
Superatom only reads. Give it a user of its own whose role may read and nothing more. As an admin (SECURITYADMIN), run the first commands below, with your warehouse and database named.

Then make its sign-in: a programmatic access token (Snowflake asks for a network policy that lets the engine's address in), or a key pair. Give the database, and the warehouse and role if they are not the user's defaults.

copy.label: A read-only role and user
Its token (copy token_secret from the answer)
Or a key pair (run in a terminal; paste the public key into the ALTER USER)
copy.value:
openssl genrsa 2048 | openssl pkcs8 -topk8 -inform PEM -out superatom_key.p8 -nocrypt
openssl rsa -in superatom_key.p8 -pubout -out superatom_key.pub
-- then, in Snowflake, with the key's body (the lines between BEGIN and END):
ALTER USER SUPERATOM SET RSA_PUBLIC_KEY = 'MIIBIjANBgkqh...';

fix.say: Snowflake accepts a token only from addresses a network policy lets in. Run the token commands above with the engine's address in the network rule, then check again.

Snowflake refused the key: the public key set on the user does not match this private key, or the user name is not the one it was set on. Set it again (ALTER USER … SET RSA_PUBLIC_KEY) and check the user name.
Snowflake refused the token: it is mistyped, expired or revoked, or restricted to another role. Make a new one (the commands above) and paste it whole.
There is no warehouse it may use. Name one, and let the role use it: GRANT USAGE ON WAREHOUSE <warehouse> TO ROLE {role}.

fix.when: does not exist or not authorized|may not use it
fix.say: There is no database {database}, or the role may not use it: GRANT USAGE ON DATABASE {database} TO ROLE {role}. Names are upper-case unless they were made in quotes.

setup.title: Which schemas
setup.say: Leave it empty to read every schema the role may see in {database}, or name the ones to read (PUBLIC, SALES). The check counts the tables it may read there.

fix.say: Signed in, but the role may read no table there. Grant it USAGE on the schemas and SELECT on their tables (the commands in the step before), or name a schema it may read.
